paras: The killing of Frank Clinton was the shooting of a Black man at Marion, Mississippi, by unknown parties, reported in July 1882. Clinton, who was said to have had two children with a white woman, was "riddled with forty-eight bullets," and the only report found gives no motive, names no attackers and records no arrests.

According to the report, Clinton, described as "colored," had for some time been "enjoying the embraces of a white woman," and the couple had two children. The item names neither the woman nor the children and says nothing else about Clinton's life or work at Marion.

At an unstated date shortly before July 20, 1882, Clinton was shot at Marion and was "riddled with forty-eight bullets" by "unknown parties." The plural wording and the number of bullets point to several shooters, but the report gives no number, no time of day and no exact location, and it does not state in so many words that Clinton died.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution appears in the coverage, and the attackers were described only as unknown.

The only account found ran on July 20, 1882, as a single sentence in the Memphis Daily Appeal's "Mississippi News" column, among items on an accidental shooting, cotton shipments, liquor fines and smallpox. The sentence carried no comment on the killing and placed Clinton's relationship with a white woman before the shooting itself, leaving readers to draw the connection. No other white paper's version and no Black-press coverage of the shooting were found.

bases: A1 reports a Black man, said to have lived with a white woman and fathered her two children, 'riddled with forty-eight bullets' by 'unknown parties' (plural), which implies a group killing with an implied racial motive, though no mob is named and no motive is stated.
Only one report was found, a one-sentence brief in A1's Mississippi news column; no local, wire or follow-up report turned up.
